items.title: Enforce run budgets (cost, runtime) in the Quarry executor, with safe org defaults
items.summary: Make quarry-edge enforce max_cost_usd and max_runtime_s on the HTTP/WS agent step path, not only max_steps. Accumulate the per-step cost that the flat action-cost table already writes into receipts on the in-memory run entry, refuse further steps with a typed budget_exhausted outcome once a cap is hit, and replace the unbounded defaults with org-level default caps. Reuse the same reserve/charge/stop pattern for crawl, batch and paid-SERP calls, and let Model Plane cost-core pass a remaining-budget figure into each browser grant.
items.whyItMatters: The product vision is 'the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects'. Today the Model can propose a budget that Quarry silently ignores, so an agent-driven browser can spend browser time and paid-provider calls without a cap. Finance and users notice runaway spend immediately, and Quarry's own docs already claim the cap is enforced.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (executor-side charge limit), with Firecrawl's reserve-then-settle for time-billed browser sessions
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Caller sets a max total charge per run. Before each billable step the executor calls charge(event, count), which returns how many units are still chargeable within the cap; when the cap is reached it finishes the current step, persists partial results and ends with a budget-exhausted status. For time-billed browser sessions Firecrawl reserves the full TTL at the per-minute rate before the first prompt (402 if the balance is short), re-rates sessions that used prompts, settles actual duration on stop and releases the remainder.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: default_constraints() is unbounded (max_steps 0, max_runtime_s None, max_cost_usd None) and the only budget check on the step handlers is enforce_step_budget(), which compares max_steps alone. The flat action-cost table computes a cost per step and stores it in the receipt, but nothing sums it or compares it with max_cost_usd. max_runtime_s only sets the lease TTL (default 120 s, agent_routes.rs:1446). AgentLoop::over_budget (agent_loop.rs:155) does check cost, but quarry-edge never calls AgentLoop (grep), so the roadmap doc's claim that max_cost_usd is enforced is not true on the production HTTP path. Crawls have page caps only. cost-core has ErrBudgetExceeded* for model spend but nothing reserves browser or crawl spend. Under ZDR receipts are not appended, so enforcement must not depend on the receipt store.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane, quarry-edge/agent_routes.rs: add spent_micro_usd and started_at to RunEntry; after each executed step add the same cost_usd already computed for the receipt (provider-billed first, flat table fallback). Replace enforce_step_budget() with enforce_budget() covering steps, cost and wall-clock, returning a typed budget_exhausted error (new ErrorCode, 429 or 402) and emitting a run event so the Model Plane planner can stop or ask for more budget. Resolve effective caps as min(request, grant claim, org default); default org caps come from the entitlement claim channel in R-t2-06-02. Model Plane: cost-core passes the remaining budget with each BrowserBroker grant and keeps one ledger key per run to avoid double counting. Then extend to crawl/batch/search: a per-job max_cost_usd that charges page and paid-provider units before dispatch.
dependencies: BrowserBroker grant issuance in production (cross-category; comparator baseline v-browser-app-083, not re-verified)
R-t2-06-02 (claim channel for org default caps)
R-t2-06-09 (cost attributes for paid providers and browser minutes)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (quarry-edge), with Model Plane cost-core supplying remaining budget
items.risks: Double counting between cost-core (model spend) and Quarry (execution spend): define one run-id ledger key. The flat table is an estimate, so budgets fail closed and may stop runs early; mark estimated vs provider-billed on receipts. Mid-run resumes must reload persisted constraints (the resume path already treats checkpoint constraints as authoritative).

alreadyPlanned.where: docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:50-53 states max_cost_usd is enforced via the flat table and AgentLoop; code on the HTTP step path does not match (doc/code divergence)

items.title: Org-owned tri-state capability policy delivered as signed claims, enforced as action-class scoped grants
items.summary: Add a per-org policy map (disabled / allowed / forced) for risky browser capabilities: raw JS evaluate, file upload and download, persistent profiles, paid search providers and ignore-robots. Deliver it to Quarry on the same signed-claim channel that already carries the ZDR floor, and have BrowserBroker mint grants that carry allowed action classes and formats (persisted, not in memory) so Quarry rejects anything outside them with a typed error. As an immediate stopgap, put raw evaluate behind default-deny plus a sensitive-approval grant like uploads, downloads and dialogs.
items.whyItMatters: Raw JavaScript evaluate currently runs on ordinary Quarry runs without approval, which undercuts the fail-closed posture of the rest of the browser stack. Admins cannot tighten what agents may do per org without a redeploy, and 'ZDR must propagate' is a per-request flag rather than a posture an org can force. This is the authority model ('Quarry executes or rejects') made concrete in code.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (per-team tri-state flags and per-key restrictions), with Codex's default-off browser gates
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl TeamFlags hold disabled|allowed|forced per capability (ZDR for scrape and search can be forced, plus ignoreRobots, threatProtection, ipWhitelist); effective option = forced ? on : (allowed ? request : reject with typed error). Keys additionally carry allowedEndpoints and allowedFormats, checked per request and cached about 60 s. Codex keeps fine-grained gates (browserUse, full CDP access, webMcp, record-and-replay, auto-auth-for-sites, multi-window) that default to off with a dev-only env override.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: ZDR already works as a forced posture (org-core RetentionPosture, a zdr JWT claim that Quarry can only raise via Claims::zdr_floor). Quarry has deny-by-default driver capabilities and sensitive approvals, but sensitive_approval_for_action covers only dialog responses, uploads and downloads (everything else returns None); AgentAction::Evaluate is implemented by the chromiumoxide and kernel drivers and executed with no approval and no org gate. BrowserBroker grants carry domains and TTL; AllowedActions exists only on sensitive child grants, ordinary grants carry no action-class or format scope, and the store is in memory. Model Plane capability-core already evaluates Allow/Deny/Ask per capability id (cap.browser.open, cap.tool.http), but nothing org-owned reaches the executor for individual risky actions.

items.approach: Control Plane: org-core owns an admin-editable capability policy ({capability_key: disabled|allowed|forced}, keys such as browser.evaluate, browser.upload, browser.download, browser.persistent_profile, search.paid_provider, crawl.ignore_robots), exposed read-only to auth-core the way retention-posture is today. auth-core adds a capability-policy claim next to zdr and Quarry's Claims struct resolves request options against it (forced overrides, disabled rejects with a typed error). Model Plane: browser-broker adds allowed_action_classes and allowed_formats to ordinary grants (persisted in Postgres or Redis), computed from the org policy intersected with capability-core's Allow/Deny/Ask decision, with escalation through the existing approval flow. Quarry: the grant validator checks action class per step; ship default-deny plus sensitive approval for Evaluate immediately, independent of the rest.
dependencies: BrowserBroker grant issuance in production (cross-category; not re-verified)
org-core policy storage and admin UI
Decide the policy of record: org-core (Control) versus capability-core (Model)
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (policy), Model Plane (browser-broker grants), Ingestion Plane (enforcement)
items.risks: Claim staleness when policy changes mid-run (mitigate with the short 15 min grant TTL and revalidation per action). Overly narrow grants can cause mid-run failures, so keep escalation through approvals. Two policy engines (org-core entitlements versus capability-core) must not diverge: pick one of record. Space access must never widen these gates.

items.title: Envelope-encrypt persisted browser profiles (and secret job inputs) per org and owner
items.summary: Encrypt Quarry browser profile snapshots (cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage) before they reach Postgres, S3 or the Redis read-through cache, using AES-256-GCM or XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a per-(org, owner) data key wrapped by a master key from env or KMS. Decrypt only inside the lease that restores the browser context. Add an isSecret flag for job inputs such as login credentials so logs, receipts and the gateway redact them.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent profiles hold live session cookies for the sites users are logged in to, so a database or backup leak is an account-takeover leak, and a Space must never be able to read them. The docs already specify encrypted snapshots but the stores write plaintext JSON. Per-owner keys also give GDPR erasure by crypto-shredding.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (secret inputs encrypted per user and Actor, decrypted only inside the run)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; unique (adopted here as a security baseline, not a feature)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: On save generate a random AES-256-GCM key, encrypt the value, wrap that key with an RSA-2048 public key unique to (user, tool) and persist ENCRYPTED_VALUE:<wrapped>:<ciphertext>. At run start the runtime receives the private key through a mounted file or env and decrypts in process; logs and stored input keep only ciphertext.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: profile snapshots are stored as a plain JSON snapshot column (PostgresProfileStore), as profiles/{org}/*.json objects (S3), and are held in a Redis read-through cache with a 3600 s TTL; no encryption code exists in any of the three. DOC: CONTRACTS.md specifies an encryption block (xchacha20poly1305 or aes-256-gcm, key from env or KMS, AAD binding org and profile) and the reliability doc lists encrypt-per-tenant plus erasure hooks, but neither is implemented. integration-corev2 has an AES-GCM vault (v1: prefix, one static key) used for connector tokens, so the pattern exists, in Go. There is no secret-field concept for job inputs.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane, quarry-runtime: add an encrypting layer at the row/object serialization boundary of postgres_profile_store.rs and s3_profile_store.rs (not above the cache) so the Redis cache holds the ciphertext envelope, or bypass the cache for snapshots. Envelope format {enc_v, key_id, nonce, aad = org|profile|snapshot, ciphertext}; data key per (org, owner) wrapped by a master key from QUARRY_PROFILE_KEY or a KMS id with key_id for rotation. Lazy re-encrypt plaintext rows on next save plus a one-off backfill migration. Wire the existing GDPR purge consumer to delete the wrapped key (crypto-shredding). Mark isSecret in the pack schema (R-t2-06-06) so receipts and gateway logs redact them.
dependencies: Master key source (env now, KMS or Control Plane key service later)
GDPR purge consumer (baseline v-quarry-101, not re-verified)
items.risks: Key rotation and loss: losing the master key destroys all profiles. Restore latency is small but the cache path must not hold plaintext. ZDR already forbids persistent profiles, so only non-ZDR rows migrate. Rust AES-GCM implementation must be new (the Go vault cannot be reused directly) and nonce handling must be reviewed.

alreadyPlanned.where: docs/CONTRACTS.md:185-199 (encryption block) and docs/SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md:134 and :289; not implemented

items.title: Procedure store and run-as-procedure, with postconditions so real runs can compile
items.summary: Persist compiled browser procedures (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped), add an execute endpoint that replays a procedure through the normal step path with grant, approval and budget checks, and offer 'save as procedure' after a successful agent run. First add optional postcondition assertions to agent steps so typical click, type and select runs can reach Verified status, because the compiler today rejects anything unverified.
items.whyItMatters: Turning a one-off agent browsing session into a repeatable, schedulable procedure is the step from 'the agent browses' to 'the product automates', and a replay is cheaper than re-planning every run. Quarry already has the hard part (compile, replay-compare, quality and impact checks) which Firecrawl's open source does not expose.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (agent run exported as skill, workflow and schema)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: GET /v2/agent/:id/skill returns {name, spec, skillMd, workflow, schema, blueprint} derived from a finished run (the generator itself is closed upstream, so only the route shape is known). Re-implement as: distill the verified action trajectory into a parameterized procedure (steps, element refs, input schema) plus a natural-language skill; store with a version; replay executes deterministic steps and hands drift back to the agent. Apify adds immutable builds numbered MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD, tag-to-build mapping and pinning, and records the resolved build on each run.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: compile_procedure, compare_replay, assess_quality and analyze_impact exist behind four stateless endpoints; the compiled procedure is returned to the caller and never stored, version is fixed at 1, and there is no execute-procedure endpoint. compile_procedure rejects any receipt whose outcome is not Verified (browser_procedure.rs:85), but outcome_for_action marks click, type, press, scroll, select and evaluate as Unknown ('postcondition_required'), so a typical form-driving run cannot compile; only navigate, wait, capture, dialog and download steps verify. Receipts are not appended under ZDR, so ZDR runs cannot be compiled at all. The Verevon UI does not call these endpoints and capability-core's skill sink does not take browser trajectories (not verified).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: (1) extend the agent step request with an optional expect assertion (URL pattern, ref present, text present) that Quarry evaluates after the action and uses to upgrade the outcome to Verified. (2) Add a procedures table (quarry-control Postgres or edge Postgres): org_id, owner_id, procedure_id, version, tags, steps, source_receipt_ids, status (draft, promoted, quarantined) and the quality report; versions are immutable, tags move, and each run records the resolved version. (3) POST /v1/agent/procedures/{id}/runs starts a run and feeds the steps through the existing step handler, so grants, sensitive approvals and budgets (R-t2-06-01) apply again; on drift return RepairRequired to the planner. Model Plane: 'save as procedure' after a successful run and register promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core (R-t2-06-07). Frontend: saved procedures list with replay-check and impact status.
dependencies: Coordinate with any automation or scheduling category
items.risks: Replaying with logged-in profiles must re-check grants and approvals every run, never replay a stored sensitive approval. ZDR runs cannot be saved. Postconditions that are too weak would let a broken replay look verified; keep the unverified-step refusal in assess_quality. Overlaps an automation category.

alreadyPlanned.where: docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:93-96 (persistent rollout state and fixture-backed quality gates for procedures)

items.title: Per-run result sets with a dataset table view and server-side export
items.summary: Give every crawl, batch and extract run an append-only result set (JSONL in the artifact store, indexed by run) behind GET /v1/runs/{id}/items?format=csv|jsonl|xlsx&fields=&omit=, with a dataset table view in the Ingestions page and a per-org retention policy. ZDR runs stream items and persist nothing. Ingestion into the Data Plane stays an explicit, selective decision.
items.whyItMatters: Users extracting structured data (prices, listings, procurement notices) need a table they can inspect, filter and export without forcing everything into the Data Plane. Today the Ingestions page shows runs, schedules, monitors, sources, evidence and profiles but no result data.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (dataset, key-value store and request queue per run)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run creation allocates dataset_id, kv_id and queue_id and injects them into the run. The dataset is append-only (items up to 9 MB) and exports server-side with format=csv|jsonl|xlsx|xml|rss, field projection (fields, omit, clean) and hidden #-prefixed debug fields. The KV store holds content-typed records for blobs and state; named storages persist indefinitely while unnamed ones expire after about 7 days; per-object rate limits return 429.

verevonToday.gap: SRC and baseline: artifact storage (memory, filesystem, S3 with content addressing), a durable Postgres URL frontier and Data Plane ingest exist, but there is no per-run result set, no dataset or key-value API, no export formats and no dataset browser; the SPA's Quarry client (quarry-client.ts) is unused code.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: at job completion write each result item to a JSONL object in the artifact store under org/run, with an index row in Postgres, and add the items route with the export formats and projection. Retention policy per org (default expiry, longer for named sets); ZDR returns items on the stream only. Frontend: dataset table view in the Ingestions run detail with an 'ingest to Data Plane' action and a download menu. Optional output schema fields arrive with R-t2-06-06.
dependencies: Optionally R-t2-06-06 for typed field metadata
items.risks: Must stay a working set with retention, not a second Data Plane (no retrieval or graph). Export of large sets needs streaming. Items can contain sensitive scraped content, so ACLs follow the run owner.

items.title: Saved job definitions: expose presets, make schedules run, then ship first-party Quarry packs with typed schemas
items.summary: Phase 1 (M): expose quarry-control's preset catalog through quarry-edge with org and Space scoping, add 'save as preset' on ingestion runs, and make scrape, crawl and batch schedules actually execute. Phase 2 (L): define a declarative QuarryPack manifest (id, version, kind, input JSON Schema with UI hints and isSecret, output schema, required driver capabilities, ZDR compatibility, cost class) and wire the existing NAV vacancies, procurement and official-statistics collectors as the first first-party packs, with a generated schema form in the SPA.
items.whyItMatters: Saved, typed job definitions give users and the Model Plane a menu of known-good jobs instead of free-form crawls, and Quarry keeps execution authority by validating (pack id, input) against the schema. It also gives dormant code (presets, collectors, schedule validation) a way to ship.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One manifest per unit (.actor/actor.json) declares name, version, build tag, env, input and output schema and default storages, and the same unit runs from the console, API, CLI, schedule or another unit. A JSON input schema with UI hints (editor, prefill, enum titles, isSecret, resource picker) renders the form and validates API input identically. Tasks are saved input plus run-option presets (up to 5,000 per user) that can be run, scheduled and shared; schedules reference presets. Codex adds an availability check (gates) before a bundled plugin is installed for a user or org.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: MountPresets is registered only on quarry-control (GET /v1/presets and /v1/presets/{name}); edge does not proxy it, so the SPA cannot reach presets, and the Rust domain preset bundles are unused. Schedules are stored and cron-validated, but control mounts the schedule lifecycle aliases with a nil Temporal client, so trigger and backfill return a typed 501, and only the change_monitor schedule kind is wired as a user-facing flow (baseline v-quarry-080, not re-verified). The NAV vacancies, procurement and official-series collectors are Go packages that nothing outside their own directories imports. The durable sources registry with monitor presets is the only user-facing preset surface. Schema-driven forms: grep of verevonv3/src for SchemaForm, schema-form, zodToForm, zod-to-json and JsonSchemaForm found nothing, so no generic renderer exists; the zod (v4) action registry shared by human UI and AI actions is the right foundation.

items.approach: Phase 1, Ingestion Plane: quarry-edge proxies control /v1/presets (read) and adds org-scoped saved presets (preset id, base preset, overrides, owner, visibility); wire a scheduler for scrape/crawl/batch kinds (the Temporal client, or a minimal control-side runner) so schedules reference presets. Frontend: 'save as preset' on ingestion runs. Phase 2, Ingestion Plane: QuarryPack manifest in quarry-core, registry in quarry-control, GET /v1/packs and POST /v1/packs/{id}/runs on edge, validated against the schema; start with the three existing collectors. Publish input and output JSON Schemas (for example schemars from the Rust types) at /v1/schemas, render them with a Solid SchemaForm, and reuse the same schema as the Model Plane tool parameters. Space-shared presets reference only sources the viewer may already see.
dependencies: R-t2-06-05 for output schema and views
OpenAPI completeness (baseline v-quarry-019: 46 of about 75 routes)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (with Frontend Plane for forms)
items.risks: Scope creep toward a third-party marketplace or arbitrary user code (sandbox isolation for browsers is absent), so keep packs declarative and first-party. Space-shared presets must not widen owner-plane ACLs. Divergence between zod and Rust schemas if both are hand-written: generate one from the other.

alreadyPlanned.where: docs/PRESETS.md and docs/SCHEDULES.md describe the preset catalog and schedule lifecycle; edge exposure and non-monitor schedule execution are not done

items.title: Offer Quarry jobs as approval-gated agent tools with cost estimates, then an off-by-default MCP facade
items.summary: Register Quarry crawl, map, batch-extract, pack runs and promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core and as Model Plane tools, with parameter schemas taken from the pack schemas. The approval card shows an estimated cost and page cap before anything runs, and new service-principal scopes gate each route. A later phase exposes the same registry through mcp-bridge as an off-by-default, org-gated MCP facade with output-token caps.
items.whyItMatters: 'AI proposes, Quarry executes' is only real if the Model can propose more than two web tools. Today the chat agent can search and fetch one URL, but crawl, extract-with-schema, packs and procedures are not agent-reachable, so the Model falls back to repeated single fetches.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Apify (natural-language runner with confirmation before paid runs)
others: Codex in-app browser (browser tooling as a small MCP server with output caps, disabled by default)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources; differentiator (the two sources use different mechanisms)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Apify: intent, then search the tool catalog (quality ranked), fill the input schema, show a confirmation with estimated cost, run, summarize the dataset; full-permission and rental tools are excluded. Codex: a minimal MCP server (js, js_reset, turn_ended) with surfaces selected by env (browser, computer or both; startup fails otherwise), tools.js.output_token_limit 25000, a startup timeout and enabled = false until the host turns it on.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: the chat agent's web tools are web_search (POST /v1/search) and web_fetch (POST /v1/extract) plus two aliases, with the scopes search:read and extract:read granted to execution-core on the Quarry audience; browser.observe only observes an existing run. Crawl, map, batch, extract-with-schema, presets, packs and procedures are not tools and carry no cost estimate. Risk-classified human approvals exist for browser actions and provider writes (stronger than Apify's single confirmation). Verevon consumes MCP servers (registry, OAuth, mcp-bridge) but exposes none; Quarry's backlog defers an MCP server because Verevon is the client.

items.approach: Model Plane: add capability ids (for example cap.web.crawl, cap.pack.run) to capability-core with Allow/Deny/Ask and risk levels; add execution-core tool definitions that map to Quarry routes using the pack and procedure schemas; the approval card shows estimated cost (R-t2-06-01 caps plus R-t2-06-09 pricing) and page limits. Control Plane: add service-principal scopes (for example crawl:write, pack:run) to the auth-core policy contract. Quarry validates and executes. Phase 2: mcp-bridge adds a Quarry MCP facade (search, fetch, extract, browser.observe/act) that always obtains a BrowserBroker grant per session, caps output tokens, and is disabled unless the org policy (R-t2-06-02) allows it.
dependencies: R-t2-06-02 policy and grants (required for the MCP facade)
items.risks: Unbounded crawls proposed by the model, so require a budget and an approval for every non-trivial job. An MCP facade that talks to Quarry directly with broad tokens would bypass the gateway authority path; it must go through BrowserBroker grants and ZDR rules.

alreadyPlanned.where: MCP server explicitly deferred in docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:112-113 (Quarry docs); agent-tool exposure has no plan found

items.title: Teach the planner the web surface: routing guidance, driver capability matrix, URL-triggered site skills
items.summary: Three small changes in one pass. (a) Replace the one-line web_search and web_fetch descriptions with narrowest-tool-first routing and freshness guidance (and the escalation path to crawl or browser) as tool descriptions plus a built-in 'web access' org skill. (b) Add GET /v1/drivers/{id}/capabilities to quarry-edge (driver by capability matrix with one-line descriptions) so execution-core builds the browser tool schema at grant time and offers a describe-capability tool. (c) Add url_patterns and an optional snapshot_scope to org agent skills so site playbooks inject when the current Quarry session URL matches.
items.whyItMatters: Cheap, measurable gains in tool choice: fewer proposals that the driver cannot execute (fewer Quarry rejections), smaller prompts, less spend, and more reliable runs on the sites customers use most. All of it informs the Model; Quarry still decides.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (capability registry with per-backend support), Firecrawl (endpoint-selection skills) and Aside (URL-triggered site skills)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources each for the three mechanisms; unique (together a differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex: the API description marks each member unsupportedByDefaultIn [backends], the agent calls capabilities.list() for {id, one line} and fetches documentation only on demand, disabled ids are not registered, and the runtime is transport-agnostic (REA: no Electron code in the parsed runtime scripts). Firecrawl: an umbrella skill plus per-endpoint skills tell agents which endpoint to use, narrowest first, kept separate from generated parameter docs. Aside: SKILL.md frontmatter {name, description, autoInject.keywords, autoInject.url, siteSpecific}; 16 site skills scope page snapshots with selectors; matched site skills are injected (bounded) and the rest are listed by name.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: web tool descriptions are one sentence each with no routing, freshness or escalation guidance. Org agent skills (session-core agent_skills with name, trigger_keywords and content) are matched by keyword overlap against the run goal at run start, at most 3 injected under a size budget; there is no URL-pattern trigger, no tab-aware injection and no snapshot scoping. Drivers declare eight deny-by-default capability booleans and gate actions fail-closed, but the matrix is only a human-readable doc (DRIVER_MATRIX.md) and not an endpoint the Model Plane reads; whether browser planner prompts adapt per driver was not verified. OpenAPI covers 46 of about 75 routes (baseline).

items.approach: Model Plane (execution-core): rewrite the tool descriptions in agent.rs and ship a built-in 'web access' skill; add url_patterns and snapshot_scope fields to AgentSkill (session-core proto and ListAgentSkills) and match against the current Quarry session URL when browser.observe runs; ship 3 to 5 first-party site skills for the sites customers use most. Ingestion Plane: expose GET /v1/drivers/{id}/capabilities (from BrowserDriverCapabilities plus the allowed action set) and complete OpenAPI so parameter docs can be generated; execution-core shapes the browser tool list from it at grant time and adds describe_capability.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (guidance, skills), Ingestion Plane (capability endpoint)
items.risks: Skill text is operator-authored prompt content: keep it out of untrusted-web channels and inside the skill budget. Capability lists must stay in sync with driver reality, so generate them from the driver trait rather than writing them by hand.

items.title: Complete web-usage metering and plan-keyed limits: browser metrics, outcome and surface attributes, per-class rate limits, per-org concurrency
items.summary: Phase A: add distinct usage metrics for browser steps and minutes, agent runs and extract/map (today extract and map are billed as search queries) with attributes {outcome, driver, llm_format, paid_provider, zdr, surface}, and a closed x-verevon-surface enum set by the gateway and Model Plane. Phase B: surface per-run usage in the ingestion run view. Phase C: add plan keys (browser agent loop, persistent profiles, concurrent sessions, schedules) in org-core entitlements delivered as claims, per-class rate limits layered on the gateway's global bucket, and a per-org fair-share concurrency cap in Quarry.
items.whyItMatters: Browser agent steps and minutes are not metered at all, so the most expensive Quarry feature is invisible to billing, and one org can consume every browser lease. Cost transparency for web acquisition (separate from model cost) and abuse protection are table-stakes that two or three of the four references have.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (single pricing function, failures free, two clear limit units)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl: one pure function price(options, outcome, cost tracking, flags) per job: base unit per page, failures cost 0, surcharges for LLM or security features, PDF per page, a ZDR surcharge, with a separate tracker of real provider costs for margin. Two limit units (pages or credits, and concurrent browsers) with separate submission and status rate limits. Aside gates features per plan (for example remote control on pro and max only). Apify meters compute units (GB-RAM-hours) plus storage operations. Every Firecrawl request also carries an origin and an integration tag from a closed list for analytics and cost attribution.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: Quarry publishes idempotent usage events to billing-core over NATS (usage.> to Lago) for five metrics (scrape page, crawl seed, search query, answer synth, batch URL), with scrape skipped on error; source is fixed to quarry-edge and there is no surface tag. /v1/extract (the web_fetch tool path) and /v1/map are metered as quarry.search.query. agent_routes.rs emits no usage events, so browser steps, minutes and agent runs are unmetered. Pricing lives in Lago billable-metric configuration outside this repo (INF, from the usage.rs comment), not in a pure function the Model Plane can call for estimates. org-core default entitlements are chat, api_keys, audit_logs and sso, quotas are api_calls, users and storage_mb per plan, and ZDR is the only computed plan-gated entitlement; no browser or Quarry keys exist. The gateway has a global distributed per-org/user token bucket (600 RPM default) over every route, but no per-class limits, and Quarry's browser pool is two or four process-wide leases with no per-org fairness. The SPA usage client is unused code.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: add metrics for browser steps and minutes, agent runs, extract and map with attributes; copy x-verevon-surface (closed enum) into usage events and receipts; emit usage from the agent step path (under ZDR carry ids and counts only, never content). Control Plane: billing-core owns the price table for the new metrics (failures free) and exposes a price-estimate endpoint that Model Plane approval cards (R-t2-06-07) and the budget work (R-t2-06-01) can call; org-core adds entitlement and quota keys that reach Quarry and the gateway as signed claims, never cross-plane DB reads. Frontend gateway: add cheap/expensive rate-limit classes on top of rate_limit.rs; Frontend: per-run usage in the ingestion run view. Quarry: a per-org semaphore in front of the lease pool, sized from the claim.
dependencies: billing-core price table and Lago metric codes
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (pricing, entitlements) with Ingestion Plane (metrics, concurrency) and Frontend Plane (rate-limit classes, usage UI)
items.risks: Pricing inside Quarry would violate plane ownership, so keep prices in billing-core and only attributes in Quarry. Usage under ZDR must carry no content. A new metric needs a matching Lago billable-metric code before it ships. Claims must flow through tokens, not DB reads.

alreadyPlanned.where: docs/BILLING.md (metering contract shipped for five metrics); browser metrics and plan keys are not planned there

items.title: Run browser evals through the production tool contract and publish per-release scores
items.summary: Drive the existing browser benchmark corpus through the same path production uses (Model Plane browser.observe and act tools, BrowserBroker grant, quarry-edge agent routes) against recorded fixture sites, score task success, steps and cost, and publish the result per release in CI.
items.whyItMatters: Agent quality regressions are caught before release only if evals exercise the real contract. Quarry's scoreboard is all pending and the Python eval-lab targets model-gateway, so the browser agent is currently benchmarked in neither place end to end.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (same runtime archives used by training and production)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The eval harness installs the same CI-published runtime version as production and drives the same tool contract against a training browser service, so scores are comparable across releases.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: Quarry lab/evals has a browser benchmark, a deterministic test site and a release-matrix binary, but the scoreboard suites are all pending. The Python eval-lab runs selftests in CI and live evals only against model-gateway with credentials. Nothing drives Model Plane browser.observe/act against quarry-edge with fixtures, so it is not established that evals cover the production tool contract.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane lab/evals: add a runner that starts quarry-edge with the test site and a stub BrowserBroker, replays recorded planner traces or a fixed small model through the Model Plane tool protocol, and emits task-success, steps and cost; add it to the quarry-v2 CI workflow as a non-live job and to a scheduled live job. Publish release_matrix output with the new scores; use recorded fixtures instead of live sites to avoid flakiness.
items.risks: Flaky live-site benchmarks (use recorded fixtures); model cost for live evals; CI runner limits for Chromium (the quarry-v2 workflow already documents build instability).

items.title: Share an agent run and its evidence with Space members through the existing resource-grant authority
items.summary: Let an owner share a finished browser or ingestion run (timeline, receipts, screenshots) read-only with named users or a Space, by adding a run resource kind to the user-core resource_grants facade that the ShareDialog already uses. The Ingestion owner plane checks the grant before serving artifacts and issues short-lived signed artifact URLs per viewer. No anonymous public links by default, and ZDR runs have nothing durable to share.
items.whyItMatters: Sharing a browsing run with its evidence is a natural collaborative feature for a workspace product, and it is what Aside's published sessions deliver. It must respect 'Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL'.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (published shared sessions with tool outputs and capped images)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Aside publishes a snapshot of the transcript plus tool outputs and up to 20 images per tool result, with explicit size caps, into an immutable share record that resolves to a read-only view. Apify adds time-limited pre-signed URLs for single objects and scoped READ/WRITE grants on chosen storages via a resource picker.

verevonToday.gap: SRC and baseline: artifacts are served only after an owner-gated gateway check and the timeline and evidence replay viewer is read-only for the owner. The gateway's ShareDialog backend proxies user-core resource_grants for documents (view-only MVP), but there is no share-run, link or signed-URL mechanism. Whether resource_grants accepts non-document resource kinds was not verified.

items.approach: User-core (or Application Plane projection): add a run resource kind to resource_grants and a Space projection of the share. Ingestion Plane: before serving receipts and artifacts, check the grant through the owner-plane ACL API and return per-viewer, short-lived signed URLs. Frontend: reuse ShareDialog on the Browser and Ingestions run views. Redact or let the owner deselect screenshots before sharing.
dependencies: resource_grants support for run resources (to verify)
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (projection) with Ingestion Plane (ACL and artifact serving)
items.risks: Apify's link sharing is ACL-widening by design and must not be copied. Screenshots can contain secrets. Grants must be revoked when the owner leaves the org.

items.title: Small contract and signal hygiene: deprecation registry, signed browser and sandbox images, web-result usefulness signal
items.summary: Three independent small tasks. (a) A typed deprecation registry and tower middleware in quarry-edge that sets Deprecation, Sunset, Link and Warning headers on retiring routes, plus a CI contract test that fails when the gateway or Model Plane call a deprecated route. (b) Sign the Quarry browser, mcp-bridge and sandbox images in CI (cosign) and verify them at deploy or admission. (c) A usefulness event per web tool result (used, ignored, failed) from the Model Plane, aggregated per domain or provider in Ingestion and fed into capability-core scoring, with no content stored under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Quarry's contracts evolve quickly while the gateway and Model Plane clients lag, browser and sandbox images handle live user sessions, and source ranking improves cheaply from a machine-readable usefulness signal. None of these is user-visible, but each is cheap insurance.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (deprecation protocol and result feedback), Codex (signed bundle receipts)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl: a typed registry {id, route matcher, deprecated_at, sunset_at, successor, message} drives Deprecation (RFC 9745), Sunset, Link rel=successor-version and Warning 299 headers plus JSON warnings, attached before auth so rejected calls still see them, with per-version request adapters; POST /v2/feedback is keyed by job id inside a short window and requires specifics on negative ratings. Codex: CI signs a receipt (RSA PKCS1 SHA256, key id, per-plugin sha256, source sha, workflow ref) and the runtime verifies it before enabling a bundle.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: Quarry exposes /v1 only, the Firecrawl-compat adapter was deleted and no Deprecation or Sunset handling was found in Quarry crates (comparator grep). A grep of .github/workflows finds no cosign, sigstore, attest, slsa, trivy or provenance step, and the Model Plane decision ledger records no cosign, SLSA or SBOM in the plane. No feedback route exists in quarry-edge/src (comparator grep); capability-core has an operator_rating input to scoring but no per-result signal from agents. Image signing could live in a deploy pipeline outside this repo, which was not checked.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: deprecation registry plus middleware in quarry-edge and a contract test in quarry-v2-ci.yml. Support Plane or CI: cosign signing and verification for the images and the mcp-bridge bundle. Model Plane: emit the usefulness event keyed by the Quarry request id; Ingestion aggregates ids and domains only; capability-core scoring consumes it.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane, with Support Plane (signing) and Model Plane (usefulness events)
items.risks: Low. The usefulness signal must not log content under ZDR (ids and domains only). The signing task needs a registry and key-management decision before it is worth doing.

dropped.reason: Duplicate of item R-t2-06-09 (per-org fair-share concurrency cap and size classes) plus the infrastructure category's distributed browser workers (baseline v-quarry-085); a raw memory knob and per-tenant warm pools are scaling work, not a platform capability to copy.

Speculative and privacy-heavy: depends on server-side web history that does not exist (history is browser-local and purged under ZDR), history and vault-title mining is invasive, and durable memory belongs to the Model Plane memory work (letta-bridge) rather than this category; revisit only with an opt-in consent design.

strengthsToKeep: ZDR is a server-computed posture (org intent AND plan entitlement) that reaches Quarry as a JWT floor that can only be raised: apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/org/types.go:273-315 and apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/auth.rs:82-140. Reuse it as the template for capability-policy claims (R-t2-06-02).

BrowserBroker grants are domain-allowlisted, TTL-bound and org/owner scoped, with single-use sensitive child approvals bound to a parent grant and revalidated per action; this is stronger than Firecrawl's API-key restrictions: apps/Model Plane/go/services/browser-broker/internal/grant/grant.go:40-110 and apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:144-300.
Fail-closed, deny-by-default driver capabilities with a backend-agnostic driver trait, the same shape as Codex's design: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:262-290.

Model Plane capability-core evaluates Allow/Deny/Ask per capability id with signed evidence before dispatch, and risk-classified human approvals cover login, checkout, posting, destructive and cross-domain actions (ahead of Apify's single confirmation): apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/capability_policy.rs and apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent/browser_risk.rs.

capability-core computes a deterministic composite tool score aimed at agent tool selection, ahead of Apify's marketplace score: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/scoring/scoring.go:1-15 (confirm Quarry tools feed it).

Org agent skills live server-side with a size budget, drop reporting, a reattach tool and a learning sink that proposes skills from sessions, which removes any need for Aside-style device sync: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/skill_budget.rs and apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/skillsink/sink.go.

Procedure compile, replay-compare, quality and impact checks already exist, beyond what Firecrawl exposes in open source: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/browser_procedure.rs:61-200.

Org tenancy is enforced end to end: the org comes from the verified session on every gateway route and Quarry uses JWT org scoping with tenant-stamped artifacts: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/auth.rs:59-140 and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/ingestions/mod.rs:1.

Search corpora go beyond Firecrawl Labs: a durable org-scoped sources registry, a local index skipped under ZDR, hybrid search with Data Plane vectors and rerank, and four SERP providers with paid-provider and ZDR switches: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/ingestions/sources.rs:47, apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/resource_routes.rs:382-731, apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/hybrid.rs:26, apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/serp.rs:372.

The gateway has a global distributed token-bucket rate limiter keyed by org, user or client IP (Dragonfly with in-process fallback), applied to every route: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/rate_limit.rs and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/main.rs:143-148.

Usage metering already flows over NATS with idempotent event ids and a failure-free rule for scrape, and a flat action-cost table with per-step receipts is the base for budget enforcement: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/usage.rs and apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/action_cost.rs.
